method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading, formula and macro comparison, reverse paraphrase and bounded primary-source terminology research; not independent or human review.
scope: All ten translated content blocks in the Dedekind-cuts section, including the definition, completeness theorem and proof, rational embedding and signed multiplication clauses.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A real point divides the real line into lower and upper parts. Dedekind constructs reals as cuts of the rationals; formally, a cut is a nonempty proper initial rational segment with no greatest member.
samples.checks: The least-upper/greatest-lower distinction, square-root example, all three cut conditions and identification of Real with the set of cuts are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Cuts are ordered by inclusion. Every nonempty upper-bounded set S of cuts has union λ as its least upper bound: λ is itself a cut, contains every member of S, and lies below any other upper bound.
samples.checks: All quantifiers, inclusions, witness steps and the common omitted-rational argument remain present. MRARITH-004 uses nonemptiness for λ's nonemptiness and boundedness for properness.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Each rational p embeds as the cut of rationals below p. Addition and nonnegative multiplication are defined by set builders; zero products are fixed explicitly, negation is defined, and strict-sign cases reduce remaining products to nonnegative ones.
samples.checks: Every source formula and commented alternative is retained under the documented 0_Real projection. The zero clause already present only in a source comment is active so all sign cases are defined.

source_observations.finding: Upper-boundedness alone does not imply that S contains a cut.
source_observations.resolution: The proof uses the explicit nonemptiness hypothesis for that inference and retains boundedness for properness.

source_observations.finding: The source has an isolated superscript zero-cut notation inconsistent with all nearby 0_Real forms.
source_observations.resolution: The Marathi formula uses 0_Real and exact QA projects that one documented correction.

source_observations.finding: The source comments out the required zero-product clause, leaving zero-factor cases uncovered.
source_observations.resolution: The source's own equation is activated in Marathi before the strict-sign cases.

limitations: No independent linguistic or mathematical certification has been performed.
